critical_code_review_comments: server.py MapUpdate.model_dump(exclude_none=True) prevents explicit reset of data_row_from/data_row_to (and any other field) to null via PATCH. If the frontend needs to clear a previously set row range, this must be handled specially — either by switching to model_dump(exclude_unset=True), by adding a dedicated 'clear' endpoint, or by using MongoDB $unset. Currently the frontend must send a sentinel or the user cannot revert to 'all rows'.

No server-side validation of data_row_from/data_row_to relationship (e.g., from <= to, both >= 1). A user could set data_row_from=100, data_row_to=1 and _build_map_rows would silently return zero rows.
No upper bound on data_row_from/data_row_to; extreme values are accepted (harmless because Python iteration handles it, but Pydantic Field(ge=1) would be defensive).

_build_map_rows uses 1-based row_num = idx + 1 where idx is 0-based over data_rows (data rows only, header excluded). This is consistent but should be documented — a user might expect 'row 1' to mean row 1 in the Excel grid (which is the header). A UI tooltip clarifying '1 = first data row after header' would prevent confusion.
server.py is now ~830 lines; prior recommendation to split into routers stands.

MapUpdate accepts data_row_from/data_row_to but there's no test that the actual /maps/{id}/data endpoint honors them at runtime (this requires MS Graph, not testable e2e). Code inspection at lines ~578-585 confirms the filter is applied correctly (row_from and row_to are 1-based inclusive, checked with 'row_num < row_from' / 'row_num > row_to').
